source.title: Generalization Guarantees for Neural Networks via Harnessing the Low-rank Structure of the Jacobian
source.authors: Samet Oymak; Zalan Fabian; Ming-Chen Li; M. Soltanolkotabi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests label corruption and training/test error on CIFAR-10, using a modified ResNet20 and error trajectories, rather than reproducing the original studies' random-label experiment in its original settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results for uncorrupted data and 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% label corruption. Other methods and findings cited from prior work are not rows. Figure-only values are recorded as figure only; the text gives qualitative descriptions but not exact plotted values.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own label-corruption sweep and training dynamics using a modified ResNet20 on three CIFAR-10 classes. These test the test-error trend in V4 and the learning order in V6, but do not establish perfect fitting of independently random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: corruption reduces label alignment with the Jacobian's information space and worsens generalization. At 50% corruption, the authors describe early learning from uncorrupted information followed by overfitting corrupted data, with the later test-error increase associated with the nuisance space.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR-10 with 3 classes and 50% corruption in its main corruption experiment; ResNet20 was modified by disabling batch normalization and softmax, and trained with least-squares loss, SGD, and data augmentation. It does not reproduce the original random-label settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Corruption fraction changes test error; for 50% corruption, test error first falls and then rises over training.
record.problems: The experiments use a modified ResNet20 and only three CIFAR-10 classes. The corruption sweep's exact values are figure-only; the paper does not state that training error becomes zero at any corrupted-label fraction, nor that test error reaches chance at 100% corruption.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results relevant to the claim were omitted. Other plotted residual projections and Jacobian alignment measures do not measure the errors named in the versions.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error and chance-level test error under completely independent random labeling, using unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters. The study changes training duration and learning-rate schedules between experiments.
The small constant-factor training-time comparison and convergence times across corruption fractions. Qualitative claims about slower nuisance-space learning do not establish these comparisons.
Perfect fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit at every corruption fraction, the chance-level endpoint, and degradation under corruption that makes labels independent of their original classes. Selected corruption fractions suffice to test the reported trend; a continuous sweep is not required.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
A separate comparison of entirely clean versus entirely random-label training trajectories, and direct accuracy trajectories for the clean and corrupted training subsets.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text does not preserve readable curve coordinates, so exact errors cannot be recovered. No failure of perfect fitting or chance-level performance can be inferred from that omission. Jacobian alignment and residual projections were explicitly declared among rows left out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report zero or near-zero training error on a completely random labeling, or test error at chance for that condition.
Does not compare training time for true versus random labels or report convergence time by corruption fraction.
Does not train on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper reports results at selected corruption fractions, not a stated continuous sweep; it does not explicitly state that training error is perfect at each fraction.
Uses standard data augmentation in its experiments but does not compare augmentation, weight decay, or dropout against their removal, or assess whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Uses 50% label corruption, not wholly random labels; the results do not compare learning dynamics across fully real-label and fully random-label training.

rows.subject: ResNet20
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on uncorrupted CIFAR-10 labels for 400 epochs; learning rate reduced at 260 and 360 epochs.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10, 3 classes; 9999 training images and 3000 test images
standard data augmentation (random crop and flip)

rows.measure: Training and test misclassification error over epochs
rows.note: The text says training and test error decrease as learning progresses; exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Valid clean-label control, but declining errors in this condition alone do not establish the corruption-dependent effect or perfect training fit. The plotted errors are minima over windows of the last 10 epochs.

rows.subject: ResNet20
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on 50% label-corrupted CIFAR-10 labels for 800 epochs; learning rate divided by 10 at 700 epochs.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10, 3 classes; 9999 training images and 3000 test images
50%; corrupted labels randomly chosen from a different class
standard data augmentation (random crop and flip)

rows.value: figure only; text says training error steadily decreases
rows.note: The text does not state that training error reaches zero or near zero.
rows.check: Steadily decreasing aggregate training error does not establish perfect fitting or distinguish clean-label learning from noise memorization by itself. It contributes to V6 when interpreted jointly with R3 and the authors' phase description. Missing confirmation of zero error is not evidence of a partial effect.

rows.value: figure only; text says test error drops rapidly at first, reaches its minimum at 100 epochs, then steadily increases
rows.note: The text attributes the later test-error increase to overfitting corrupted data.
rows.check: The early test-error decrease and subsequent increase, interpreted alongside R2, support the authors' clean-information-first, corrupted-data-later account. This trajectory across epochs does not directly measure V4's test-error trend across corruption fractions. Remove the spurious numbers_found value '1/1'; the stated minimum occurs at 100 epochs.

relationships.condition: Modified ResNet20 on three CIFAR-10 classes, with 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% strictly different-class label corruption, evaluated after 800 epochs
relationships.reason: The authors explicitly report increasing test error with corruption level in R4–R7. This supports the degradation component; perfect training fit and a chance-level endpoint remain untested.
relationships.display_finding: Test error increased with corruption level after 800 epochs of training.

relationships.condition: Modified ResNet20 trained with SGD and 50% label corruption
relationships.reason: R2–R3 show declining training error while test error reaches a minimum at 100 epochs and then rises; the text attributes the early phase to clean information and the later phase to overfitting corrupted data.
relationships.display_finding: Test error reached its minimum at 100 epochs and then rose while training error continued falling, which the authors attributed to later corruption overfitting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Test error decreases during training without corruption (R1), rises after an early minimum with 50% corruption (R3), and the authors state test error increases as corruption rises across the tested fractions (R4–R7). The paper does not establish perfect training fit at each fraction.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe an initial phase learning information in uncorrupted data, followed by overfitting corrupted data as test error rises (R2, R3).
